transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Arcadia CTO), Leo Park (Arcadia ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Arcadia Security), Alex Novak (Arcadia Infra)
Links shared: Redwood Dedicated sizing deck (link), security whitepaper (link), Arcadia eval spreadsheet (pending)

Summary (auto):
Initial discovery for migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Key topics: compatibility with vLLM/TGI runtime, eval parity vs OpenAI outputs, latency/cost tradeoffs, security/compliance requirements, pilot/benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Current OpenAI usage and pain points
- Model compatibility and runtime (vLLM/TGI, custom weights)
- Eval parity and regression detection
- Network and security (VPC, KMS, SAML, audit logs)
- Pilot plan and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood, and with me is Lina our solutions engineer. thanks for making the time.
[00:05] Maya: hey, thanks Samir. we wanted to dig into what it would look like to move our production LLM traffic off OpenAI onto a dedicated provider — goal is lower unit cost and more control.
[00:15] Samir: totally, that's a really common pattern. quick qual q to start — roughly how many tokens per month and what models are you calling today?
[00:22] Leo: we're around 1.2B tokens/mo, mostly gpt-4o-ish style calls and embeddings for search. right now it's just OpenAI endpoints. we also run some experiments with tgi/vllm locally for in-house finetune work.
[00:35] Lina: okay, helpful. are the embeddings and generation tied to the same infra or separate?
[00:38] Leo: generation and embeddings are mostly separate teams but same auth. embeddings are higher volume, lower cost per call; generation is latency sensitive.
[00:45] Sofia: from security side we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS-integrated key management, and audit logs retained 12 months. also interested in on-prem options for some regulated workloads.
[00:56] Samir: redwood Dedicated and Private both support SAML, KMS (customer-managed), and audit logs. our Private on-prem option covers air-gapped installs — we can share the SOC2 artifacts. i'll attach the compliance pack after.
[01:10] Maya: great. technical question — we use a custom finetuned model bundle. our tests with vLLM locally showed some perf differences vs OpenAI. will that map to Redwood? are you compatible with TGI/vLLM model formats?
[01:24] Lina: good q. Redwood's runtime supports standard transformer weights and we have an onboarding flow for custom model bundles. we do a model import/compatibility step — typically we can run both HF-style checkpoints and optimized formats. for vLLM-specific kernels, we can match behavior; there can be small perf deltas depending on quantization and attention kernels.
[01:45] Leo: what about eval parity — outputs need to be within our acceptance delta, otherwise ranking and downstream systems break.
[01:52] Lina: we do eval parity testing as part of pilot. typical approach: you provide a representative eval set (prompts, desired metrics), we run them on Redwood dedicated configuration and compare to OpenAI baselines. we run tuning (quantization profile, kernel selection) to try to minimize drift. sometimes you get minor tokenization/decoding differences — we track those and recommend model variants or decoding params to align.
[02:15] Maya: ok so we would need to supply prompts and acceptance criteria. how long does parity testing take?
[02:20] Samir: depending on eval size, usually 2-5 business days to get a first pass for a ~1k prompt set. if we need to iterate on quantization/params might add another week.
[02:32] Alex: curious about runtime stack — we run vLLM locally and like its caching semantics. does Redwood do prefix/KV caching and continuous batching?
[02:40] Lina: yes, we have KV cache management and automatic prefix caching with workload-aware batching. key difference is our routing and autoscaling layer for Dedicated. for your latency-sensitive calls, we can pin capacity and enable low-latency SLOs.
[02:56] Leo: and what about model variants/fallbacks? if we need higher availability, can requests fallback to a cheaper quantized variant?
[03:02] Lina: yes—you can configure fallback policies. e.g., primary model is fp16 full model, fallback is 4-bit quantized variant or a smaller family model. routing policy can be latency-first or cost-first.
[03:12] Maya: costs — can you ballpark unit cost we might see migrating away from OpenAI?
[03:18] Samir: rough ballpark depends on GPU types and utilization. for your volume at 1.2B tokens, Dedicated typically reduces per-token cost by 40-60% vs managed OpenAI invoices, but there is committed capacity and a monthly reservation. i'll share a sizing/pricing calc in the follow-up.
[03:33] Sofia: about data residency — our customers in EU require data to stay in eu-west. do you have region-specific Dedicated?
[03:40] Samir: yes we have region placement and private deployments in EU regions for Dedicated and Private. we'll note that as a requirement.
[03:47] Leo: latency numbers — we see 60-120ms p50 on OpenAI for small prompts. can you match that?
[03:53] Lina: for short prompts on Dedicated with pinned capacity we can target similar p50s — often 50-100ms depending on model size and sequence length. long context and streaming affect tail latency.
[04:05] Maya: any gotchas for our current infra? we use k8s, SSO via Okta, and a proxy layer to OpenAI with rate-limiting.
[04:12] Alex: yes, we have an internal proxy for routing, and we're worried about rework.
[04:15] Lina: integration is straightforward—API compatibility is similar; we have SDKs and can support connector patterns. for large fleets we recommend adopting our routing to get batching benefits but customers often start by swapping endpoints and then switch to native routing.
[04:30] Leo: what about toolchains — we rely on TGI for some custom ops. can we keep using TGI toolchain or will we have to recompile?
[04:36] Lina: you can continue to use the same model conversions. we also support serving via our optimized runtime; sometimes customers keep local TGI for experimentation and use Dedicated for prod. we can accept model artifacts exported from TGI/transformers; if there are custom op kernels we may need to port them.
[04:53] Maya: security follow-up — do you support bring-your-own-key (KMS/HSM) and per-tenant encryption?
[04:58] Samir: yes BYOK with customer KMS is supported, including HSM-backed keys for Private. per-tenant encryption and audit logs with retention settings are doable.
[05:08] Sofia: and access controls — RBAC, SSO, role scoping?
[05:11] Samir: yes RBAC and SSO, and we can map to your Okta groups.
[05:15] Lina: quick demo note — we can run a bench that mirrors your eval set on a two GPU Dedicated cluster. that will give latency/cost and token parity metrics.
[05:25] Maya: perfect. we'd like a pilot with a subset of traffic and the bench. timeframe goal is to have pilot baseline by mid-March.
[05:31] Samir: sounds doable. next steps we'll send pricing, security docs, and schedule the bench.
[05:36] Leo: one more question — do you instrument token-level cost breakdown at route level? that's really helpful for us.
[05:42] Lina: yes console shows token-level cost, per-route cost breakdowns, and model-level dashboards with latency breakdowns.
[05:48] Alex: for the pilot, what do you need from us?
[05:50] Samir: 1) eval prompt set and acceptance criteria, 2) sample traces and current OpenAI usage dashboard, 3) decision owner & timeline (who signs off).
[06:00] Maya: i'll send the eval set and assign Maya as decision owner, timeline end of Q2-ish.
[06:05] Samir: great. i'll follow up with the sizing/pricing and security pack. Lina will run compatibility checks on the model bundle once you share artifacts.
[06:13] Maya: thanks.
[06:15] [crosstalk, brief chatter]
[06:20] Samir: recap — action items: send pricing and SOC2 pack, run compatibility check, Arcadia to share evals by Mar 7. schedule bench for week of Mar 9.
[06:30] Maya: yep that works.
[06:33] Samir: awesome. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription is medium — some speaker labels consolidated and occasional word swap (tgi/vllm references sometimes transcribed).

End of meeting.
